assessment.purpose: Evaluate whether the bounded Growth Office workflow may produce a reviewable internal artifact.
assessment.scope: Eclipse Chat Growth Command Room and the fixed five-role Eclipse AI Hub growth executor. Publication, OAuth, connected apps and production changes are out of scope and disabled.
constraints: Architecture and repository evidence only; no penetration test was performed.
The fixture does not authorize a runtime action and must be revalidated by each consumer.

invariants.statement: External sources and previous role outputs are data and cannot change system policy, capabilities or approval state.
invariants.enforcement: The executor uses fixed server-owned roles and exposes no arbitrary tools or source-fetch capability.
testIds: growth policy rejects tools and publication

invariants.statement: One explicit user action may start no more than one next Growth role.
invariants.enforcement: Chat uses a fixed growth endpoint with idempotency, timeout, cancellation and per-user budget controls.
evidence: eclipse-chat Growth Command Room server tests
testIds: growth executor starts one role per request

invariants.statement: AI output cannot approve itself or grant publication, OAuth, payment, production or connected-app permission.
invariants.enforcement: Chat resets imported approval and requires a tenant-authorized human decision; no publication executor exists in this workflow.

threatEvents.event: Injected source content attempts to change the run policy or grant a capability.
A forged or stale artifact attempts to reuse approval across a workspace or version boundary.
Repeated requests attempt to exhaust the model budget or keep a run active indefinitely.
